trails.sourceDescription: Updates are provided directly by trail maintainers.
trails.notes:
Store to purchase Battle Creek swag! https://lifebrand.co/store/brand/my-brand/battle-creek-mtb-st-paul/

Battle Creek Rec Center Trailhead (75 Winthrop St S). Quickest way to the singletrack is up the hill South of the Rec Center.  Follow the looping Cat Walk trail up to the entrance of the Higher Ed singletrack. 

Another trail entrance is on Battle Creek Road between Upper Afton Rd and Lower Afton Rd.  Look for the singletrack signs, and there's usually cars parked nearby.  From here you can access the trails above the Rec Center, and also the trails along the bluff (like Wall of Death) and get access to the Overlook trail. 

(Note: there is another parking lot available off Pt. Douglas Road - we don't recommend using it, as there have been quite a few break-ins at the Pt. Douglas lot.)

Battle Creek offers quite an extensive network of trails, as compared to most metropolitan trail systems. In many areas of the park, it's easy to forget you're surrounded by suburbs on all sides. Battle Creek has something for riders of all technical abilities, with trails running the gamut from smooth, hard-pack ski trails to expert-level singletrack. The terrain is quite hilly, so expect the trails to give you a good workout. Although hilly, the climbs tend to be relatively short, with the longest single climb gaining approximately 110' in elevation. Trails are mainly fast hardpack, with a few sandy sections and a few rocks & roots.

trails.description: Precipitation is making for some soggy trails.  Please stay off trails until things have dried out, thank you.
trails.sourceDescription: Updates are provided directly by trail maintainers.
trails.weatherPolicy: Please do not ride the trail when it is wet/muddy.  If you are leaving marks in the trail or your tires are picking up a lot of dirt, it is too wet to ride.  Trail generally needs 12-24 hours to dry after a rain event (depending on rainfall amount and time of year).
trails.notes:
Two parking areas are available, the south entrance off 90th street, provides users access to 4 miles of hiking trails, 14 miles of single track mountain bike trails, an access to Bertram Lake and  a carry-in access to Long Lake which will allow users the opportunity to paddle Long, Mud and First Lakes

The main park entrance is located at 9842 Briarwood Avenue NE, Monticello MN on the North end of Bertram Lake, this entrance provides users access to the swimming beach, hiking trials, picnic facilities, picnic shelter (available for reservation), and a four season climate controlled chalet, and Camp Manitou facilities/day camp.

trails.notes: Parking only at designated trailhead locations. Multiple segments of trail system linked by paved shared use trail.

trails.description: Conditions should be great today especially later in the day. There is a tree down on Shore Shimmy. Use caution. The trail crew will remove that this evening.
trails.sourceDescription: Updates are provided directly by trail maintainers.
trails.ebikePolicy: Electric bicycles (e-bikes) that meet the definition of "electric-assist bicycle" in MN Statue 169.011 are allowed on the trail. Motorized bicycles and other electric cycles (e.g. e-motos) are not allowed on the trail.
trails.weatherPolicy: Please monitor trail conditions before heading out. We recommend waiting at least 12-24 hours (in some cases more) after a rainfall. When riding if you are sinking in and leaving tire ruts or foot print impressions, we ask that you do not ride and hop off the trail. Thank you!

trails.sourceDescription: Updates are provided directly by trail maintainers.
trails.notes: Cottage Grove Bike Park is open dawn till dusk, weather permitting, and includes a 4x track, two pump tracks, and a complete dirt jump plaza.

newsItems.title: Lebanon Hills Sustainable Trails Study
newsItems.content:
Have you noticed the orange and white flags while out on the trails in Lebanon Hills Regional Park? Those are part of the [Lebanon Hills Sustainable Trails Study](https://www.co.dakota.mn.us/parks/CurrentProjects/Pages/sustainable-trails.aspx "Lebanon Hills Sustainable Trails Study") for possible trail re-alignments (orange) and emergency access routes (white with blue dots). The current flagged routes are tentative and subject for review. We (MORC volunteers maintaining the MTB trails) are working with park staff to minimize impacts with the mountain bike trails and provide our feedback on route alignments. 

*FYI - Buckthorn removal is tentatively scheduled for the western park section this fall / winter. MTB trail access might be impacted. This is a separate project from the trail study, more details to come.*

eventItems.title: Lebanon Hills Trail Work
eventItems.content:
Lebanon Hills has trail work sessions nearly every Tuesday through summer. Details on specific tasks for the evening will be added a day or two prior to the work session. Come out and spend the evening throwing dirt, moving rocks, or rolling logs while talkin' about your dream bike. 

No experience needed, nor anything to bring, we provide the tools and direction on tasks for the evening. We just recommend wearing something that can get dirty (pants and sturdy shoes/boots suggested) and other personal protective items like gloves and glasses. Waivers need to be signed and safety speech before trail work begins is required.

eventItems.title: Lebanon Hills Grill-Out 🍔
eventItems.content: Each summer we have one Tuesday evening where we skip throwing dirt, rolling logs & lifting rocks to instead grill burgers, enjoy BYOB & BS the night away. We provide the burgers with all the fixin's, chips & cookies. Those with special food requirements should reach out on the email list or comment here to get in touch with us. More details to come, sometimes there is a pre-ride. **This is an invite event for those who attended at least one trail work session for the season**, so be sure to get a trail work session in before mid-summer! Please RSVP here so we know how many burgers to get.
